quick_english: Sanjaya says that seeing the Pandava army arrayed, King Duryodhana approached the teacher and spoke.
cite_parts: sañjaya uvāca   dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā

quick_english: Duryodhana asks the teacher to look at the great arrayed army of Pandu's sons, arranged by Drupada's wise son, his disciple.
Here are heroes and great bowmen equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great chariot-fighter.
Dhrishtaketu and Cekitana, the valiant king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, best of men.
Yudhamanyu and valiant Uttamaujas, Saubhadra, and the Draupadeyas—all indeed great chariot-fighters.
But know, best of the twice-born, the distinguished leaders among us, for naming my army's commanders to you.
cite_parts: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama
nāyakā mama  sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te

quick_english: In the great army, all these hero-approved leaders are: you, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Shalya, Jayadratha, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and valiant Saumadatti.

quick_english: What use is this enumeration? Our force, protected by Bhima, is insufficient; but their force, protected by Bhishma, is sufficient. The Pandava force protected by Bhimasena is ours and insufficient to conquer; or the force protected by Bhishma is related to these Pandavas and sufficient to conquer, if much is not conquerable by them in battle.

quick_english: Stationed in all passages according to your portions, you all indeed must protect Bhishma.
Causing joy in him, the valiant Kuru elder and grandsire roared loudly and blew the conch.
Then conches, drums, paṇavas, anakas, and gomukhas were struck all at once, and that sound became tumultuous.
Then Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava, standing in the great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.
Hṛṣīkeśa blew Pāñcajanya, Dhanañjaya blew Devadatta, and Vṛkodara of terrible deeds blew Pauṇḍra, the great conch.
King Yudhiṣṭhira, Kuntī's son, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.
Kāśya, the supreme archer, Śikhaṇḍin, the great chariot-fighter, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa, and the unconquered Sātyaki.
The Pāñcāla great archer, the five Draupadeyas, and mighty-armed Saubhadra each blew conches separately.
That sound tore the hearts of Dhartarashtra's sons and resounded tumultuously through sky and earth.
Then, seeing Dhartarashtra's sons arrayed and weapons begun to clash, the monkey-bannered Pandava raised his bow.
Then Arjuna spoke this word to Hrishikesha: O lord of earth, place my chariot between both armies, O Acyuta.
cite_parts: arjuna uvāca   senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta

quick_english: Until I see these standing eager to fight, with whom by me must be fought in this battle effort.
I wish to see those who will fight, who are assembled here, desiring to please evil-minded Dhartarashtra in war.
Sanjaya said: thus addressed by Gudakesha, O Bharata, Hrishikesha placed the best chariot between both armies.
cite_parts: sañjaya uvāca   evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata

quick_english: Arjuna said, O Partha, see these gathered Kurus led by Bhishma and Drona.
There Partha saw standing fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
Fathers-in-law and friends were also in both armies.
Seeing all those kinsmen standing there, Arjuna was overcome by supreme compassion, sank down, and said this.
Arjuna said, seeing these kinsmen eager to fight, Krishna, my limbs sink and my mouth dries up.
cite_parts: sīdanti mama  gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati

quick_english: Trembling and hair-standing arise in my body; Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns.
I cannot stand steady, my mind reels, and I see reversed omens, Keśava.
cite_parts: na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ

quick_english: I see no good in slaying kin in battle; I do not desire victory, Kṛṣṇa, nor kingdom and pleasures.
What is kingdom to us, Govinda, or enjoyments and life, when those for whom we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures are to be slain?
cite_parts: yeṣāmarthe  kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca

quick_english: Those standing in battle, abandoning lives and wealth, are teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers.
cite_parts: ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca

quick_english: I do not wish to kill these kin, even for three-worlds sovereignty or earth; the opponent's view is stated before the answer.

quick_english: Having slain the Dhartarashtrans, what joy would there be, O Janardana?

Sin would cling to us if we killed these aggressors; therefore we are not fit to kill our Dhārtarāṣṭra relatives. In such killing sin alone is the agent; our enemies are already subdued by sin, and killing them along with ourselves would bring sin. Here sin comes from greed and from failing to see faults such as the destruction of family.
